title: Hired and fired in seven hours

chapters.headline: Hired and fired in seven hours: the Braiden Bell mess and the Dundon pattern
Lillard and Morant in the same backcourt: does it work, and who starts?
Spurs bottom and winless on £380m, with the City verdict hanging over everyone
Verstappen on pole in Sepang while upgraded Mercedes stumbles
USMNT vs Mexico: Adams gets the armband and Pochettino needs a rivalry win

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack Vernon. You're on.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm on. Are you chewing?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Breakfast burrito. One second. Okay. So yesterday I tell my nephew, meet me in the lot by the Kinko's.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Oh no.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: There's no Kinko's. There hasn't been a Kinko's on that corner for, I don't know, a decade? He sends me a photo of a dispensary with a question mark.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So you're giving directions to a city that doesn't exist anymore.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm giving directions to 2014. Two years home and I'm still a tourist with a really old map.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: For what it's worth, in my head the arena is still the Rose Garden.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Everybody's is. The building keeps changing its name and we just refuse.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Meanwhile the new TV guy didn't stick around long enough for anybody to learn his name.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Hired at noon Thursday. Gone by dinner.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Seven hours, give or take.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, gut first. Firing him was right. Those posts are ugly, and one of them was about Asian people, and, look, I'm a Japanese-American kid from a family that's been in this city for generations. That one I felt in my chest. I'm not going to pretend I read it like a neutral guy.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: No, you shouldn't.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: But then I did the math. Those posts are from 2012, 2013. He was fifteen. A high school freshman. He's twenty-nine now. I sat with that for a minute, and I still don't know exactly where I land on him as a person.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm very glad nobody can scroll back through me at fifteen. Very glad.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. What was fifteen-year-old Jack like?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Bad haircut, worse opinions, and luckily no internet. Nora, though. I'll admit something. I check what she posts.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I know. She's a good kid, and I'm not worried she's cruel. What I worry about is some dumb thing she types at nineteen that somebody pulls up when she's twenty-nine and up for a job. Which is exactly this. So I came into this one less sure than I'd like.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's the first time you've told me you lurk on your daughter.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Don't tell her. Anyway. The firing I can live with. What I keep chewing on is who found it. A reporter at a local TV station found it. The team didn't. Was it anybody's job to spend one afternoon scrolling back through this guy?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You'd do that for a guy running trivia night at the bar. Ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, but did they skip it, or run a lazy one and miss stuff from 2012? Those are two different problems. One you fix with a checklist. The other means nobody upstairs thought it mattered.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And we don't know which.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: We don't. Their apology had a line, 'We did not meet our own bar in this process.' Which, honestly, is plainer than I expected from them.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Can I argue the weird side for a second? I think the seven hours is the one thing they did right.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Go.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Every other thing this ownership touches, it drags. The July firings, the arena talk, and that's where I go cold, by the way. The team belongs to the city, and I don't love anybody pointing at the city's wallet. But this? They found out, they owned it, they apologized to Rip City by name, done by evening. The fast part was the competent part.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Hm. Yeah. Okay, I'll give you that one. The cleanup was the most decisive thing I've seen out of that front office.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Which is a pretty sad sentence.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Here's what I'd add, though. You're hiring in a hurry, a week before preseason. In my experience the homework is the first thing a cost-cutting building squeezes. I can't prove that's what happened. It just fits.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It stings because it fits. And the guy who pays for it is a young broadcaster, while whoever skipped the check keeps their badge.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's the part I hate. Every time I've seen it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'll criticize the process all day. I'm leaving him alone. He hasn't said anything yet. I hope someday he gets to.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So tell me about the Benetti thing. You laughed when people started begging for him.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I laughed and winced. I don't know if it's realistic. But I think what fans want is a voice that sounds like it's staying. Somebody who'll be there for the worst losses, the voice you hear in your head when you're eighty. My dad yelled at refs over that broadcast every road game for thirty years. That's a lot of trust to hand a stranger, and this ownership hasn't earned any.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So it's a trust vote.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Basically, yeah.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Then the Fan Fest question. Can they get through Sunday clean? My bar is on the floor. Hold the event, nobody says anything strange into a microphone.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Mine's a little higher. Kids on the court, a decent scrimmage, and by Monday the headlines are about basketball. Okay, that's the optimism talking.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's the optimism winning the whole argument.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Fine. Basketball. You've got a crowded guard room and a first-year coach. Give me three lineups, worst to best. Guards and Deni only, assume a real center back there for now.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Assume a center. Love the confidence. Okay. Number three: Dame, Ja, Jrue, Deni. The closing group. It's good! It's also two thirty-six-year-olds, and it's the exact thing I'm scared of. The kids' minutes get traded for feeling safe.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Noted. Two.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: The starting group everybody expects. Dame, Ja, Shaedon, Deni. Three guys who've always had the ball, I know. But Dame said it himself, he's a shot-maker, he can live off the ball. And nobody leaves Dame in the corner.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Walk me through that, though. Who cuts? None of those guys has ever been the role player.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ja. Here's the picture in my head. Dame comes off a high screen, two guys jump him because everybody always jumps Dame, and Ja's guy turns his head for half a second. Ja's already gone, backdoor, baseline, ball's in the air. That dunk has been sitting in his legs for years and Memphis never had the setup for it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And when they don't turn their heads? Thirty-one point one from three for his career. Never above thirty-four in a season.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Then he has to make the open one. That's the bet. A guy adding something new at twenty-seven, I'm in.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay. Number one.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Scoot's unit. Scoot with the ball, Jrue next to him as the adult in the room, Shaedon getting shots. For a twenty-two-year-old that beats being the fourth guy who wants the ball in a starting five. Every trip, his ball, against backups. I'm telling you, that's the March version of Scoot.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Every kid you love is two years away and different in March.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And someday I'll be right and it'll be unbearable. Your turn.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I've got one. And it breaks my own rule. Take the center off the floor. Dame, Ja, Jrue, Shaedon, Deni at the five.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Deni at the five? Who's rebounding? Who's at the rim?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Deni, and nobody, for six minutes. But listen to your own story. Your backdoor cut needs an empty paint. A center's guy is standing right where Ja wants to land. Pull him out, five guys who can dribble, and Ja's cut is wide open every trip.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ugh. You used my dunk against me.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It was a good dunk.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, for the Ja cut, that's actually the best version of it. I'll give you that. But you've got two thirty-six-year-olds chasing guys bigger than them, and a guy who just told me he's never been a role player now playing center. One bad rebounding stretch and Nori's calling timeout.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Six minutes. Start of a fourth quarter, when the other team's got its own center sitting.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Six minutes I'll sign. You were going to say it closes games.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I was absolutely going to say it closes games.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. And Shaedon, honestly, I flip on him every day. Fourth starter some days, the scorer in Scoot's group other days. Nori keeps saying it's all about combinations. I think he doesn't know yet either.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, verdict. Name the one the other guy ranked too high.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Yours, past six minutes. Every minute past that comes out of Scoot's year.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Your Scoot unit at number one. You ranked a feeling.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I ranked a feeling with a jump shot.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. Golden State, Wednesday, ten Eastern. I'm watching whether Nori ever goes small.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm watching Ja when he doesn't have it. Hey, quick one for you: did you ever get your bookshelves the way you want?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Third arrangement. By color now. Don't.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: By color. Okay. My dad's all over this stuff, by the way. He watched one camp clip, said 'one ball,' held up one finger, and asked my mom where the remote was. She was holding it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Of course she was.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: He's counting Sundays till the season starts. I'm sort of counting them too. Different reasons. Anyway, he wants Jrue on the floor at the end. You two would get along.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Tell him I said he's right.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Absolutely not.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Can I do Spurs before you enjoy it too much?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I would never.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Bottom of the table. No win in five. Ten new signings this summer and still nothing. Tom, you know this feeling. A Spurs start where you can't even enjoy being mad because there's too much to be mad about.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So which one gets you more? City guilty on basically everything, appeal lodged Thursday night, a whole decade that looks rigged. Or your own club, bottom? I figured. I think it's the same fire, though.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Go on.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Spurs haven't turned a profit since 2019. No European money this year. Their own CEO says the financial rules are a genuine constraint, so they have to get better at selling players. So they sold. Including that teenager to Brighton.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Vuskovic. Don't.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So this whole summer got built around rules City just got found guilty of breaking for years. The breaking back then is part of why your club is selling teenagers now.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ugh. Okay. That's annoying, because now I have to be angry at both at the same time.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Welcome to being a Spurs fan, I assume.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. Ten years of watching Son at four in the morning in a Shibuya bar, and then he leaves for LA, and I came home thinking at least the misery would be on my time zone.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And now it's on your time zone and worse.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Way worse. And the line from the club is 'underlying performances.' Chances against Newcastle, Forest, Everton, nothing going in. I'm sympathetic! Ten new signings, and Romero, Vicario, Palhinha, Danso, Spence all gone. That's a whole spine. A group like that needs reps.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: When a board says 'underlying performances' in October, I hear a board that can't afford to change course yet.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Cold.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Maybe it's true too. I just want to hear what they say if it's still zero in November.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Chances and no goals is something you can say for about three weeks. Then it's just who you are.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So the break. Time, or a deadline with a nicer name?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I want it to be time. Time together on the training ground is the one thing that group is short on. And they rebuilt the whole medical and fitness side because of all the injuries. Let that settle.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I think it's a deadline. A winless start just sits there for two weeks with nothing to change it. Every pundit gets a fortnight to sharpen.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Win the first game back and the break was a gift.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Lose and it was a countdown. Okay, who are you angrier at when they go a goal down in the first twenty minutes? Honestly.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Honestly? Me. For still setting the alarm.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Speaking of alarms. Formula One, Sunday. Four a.m. for me.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: One a.m. for me, and I'll be up. In Tokyo, F1 was a normal-hour sport. Sunday afternoon, a little bar near my apartment, a guy behind the counter who'd go silent for the last ten laps and then pour everybody a drink when it was over, whoever won. I got hooked on the room before I understood the racing.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So you watch for the bartender.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I watch because of the bartender. Anyway. Max on pole, his first since Abu Dhabi last December. And the upgraded Mercedes falls on its face.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Which is your kind of story.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It's every young Blazers lineup I've ever defended. The upgrade looks better on paper, and then you check the lap times and go, hmm.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. And there's no clean test for it. You can't bolt the old car back on and run it again.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So is Red Bull back, or is this one weird track?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Everybody's blaming the asphalt. Sounds like it's rough out there, and the lap times are way off what they used to be.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's where I am, honestly. Tyres get eaten, the order gets shuffled, Singapore next week tells us the truth.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I started there too, and I can't make it hold. Mercedes is losing time to Max on the straights, and the straights don't care about tyres. That's the car. Something else is going on there. So I'll split it. Red Bull's genuinely better than they were, and Sepang makes it look bigger.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Huh. Okay, the straights thing gets me. I'll move. Red Bull's real, a little.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: A little. And they get a gift on top, Hadjar's up there and an engine-part penalty drops him down the grid.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Which helps Antonelli. Title in trouble, though?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I don't think so. He's still the one with the points lead, and he's the one who got the clean side of the grid today.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And Antonelli's the kid who got better today. Car doesn't know what it is, and he still squeezes out the clean side of the grid.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And then he talks like an accountant. 'If we have to settle for P3, P4, we'll take that.' Very calm for a kid.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Meanwhile Norris, the reigning champion: 'We're just slow.' I respect that. No spin.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's a guy who's tired of watching his car lose on every straight.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: But my one a.m. guy is Hamilton. Front row in a Ferrari, and he sounds like a grown man who's happy as a kid. I'll take that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So that's who you're losing sleep for.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I'm up at one a.m. rooting for a guy who's happy. My bartender would approve.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Before your Hamilton date, U.S.-Mexico in Arizona tonight. With a new captain.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Tyler Adams. I love it, honestly. He's a craftsman. Does the unglamorous work in front of the back line and never asks for credit. He already wore it in Qatar. It feels right.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: My worry's different. He and Pochettino are close. Two years of talking every week. Does a captain who already knows exactly what the coach wants ever push back when it counts?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Okay, but isn't that the whole point of giving him the armband? A captain who can stand up to the coaches.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Coaches always say that. I've hired people who were told to challenge me. Took them about a year to try.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. Okay, fair. Year one, though, you want the guy who works with the staff. The pushing back comes once the room trusts him.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And somebody asks if Adams is captain through 2030, and Pochettino goes, 'If he behaved well.'

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Great line. My only real worry is the body. He plays the position that gets kicked, and he's got to stay on the field for four years.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, the game. Does beating Mexico matter for Pochettino as much as everyone's saying?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Less, I think. It's a friendly. Treat it like a rehearsal, mix vets and kids, see who holds up in a building that's mostly green. But I could flip on that by halftime.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I was right there with you, and then I moved a little. Mexico beat you in the Gold Cup final. They won the Nations League too. They've got the bragging rights. Lose tonight and that follows them home, and every bad half for the rest of the window gets read through it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: So it shouldn't matter, but it will.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And Pochettino doesn't get to decide which.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Yeah. That's probably right. Márquez needs it more, though. Everybody's got their eyes on the other bench, and I think he knows it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Smart. All the pressure lands on the other bench. And Gil Mora's cleared after the ankle.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Seventeen, with a building full of noise on him. That's what I'm tuning in for. Who looks scared in the first ten minutes, on both sides.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I've got a soft spot for anybody trying to lead a bunch of young players. I've been watching a frankly unreasonable amount of Oregon football.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Because Nora texts you about it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's the one thing she texts me about. It's a funny feeling, wanting to be useful to kids who are doing completely fine without you.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack. That's the guy who checks her posts, by the way. Same guy.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Yeah. I heard it as I said it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Call her after the game.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: She'll be out. It's Saturday night, she's nineteen.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Then text her a score. That's how she'll know you're watching.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay. Fine. I'll text her a score. Tonight Mexico, Sunday Fan Fest, Wednesday the Warriors.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And one a.m. Hamilton in between. Tom, thanks for hanging out. We'll see you after Golden State.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Go find a Kinko's, Mikey.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: There are no Kinko's, Jack. That's the whole point.
